sources.title: Setting up and managing prepaid API billing
sources.retrieval: web search tool, 2026-09-09. The search returned this article's TITLE, URL and a page age of July 30, 2026. It did NOT return the article's text: the persisted result contains result metadata only, with no page content. Direct HTTPS fetch of help.openai.com returns HTTP 403 to automated clients (refusal page retained as prepaid_help_403_refusal.html).
establishes: An article titled 'Setting up and managing prepaid API billing' exists at this URL.
Its page age was reported as July 30, 2026, so the work order's URL is live and current.
Three adjacent help-centre pages exist: 8264778 'What is prepaid billing?', a redirect-titled 8264644 variant, and the collection 3943089 'Account, login and billing'.
does_not_establish: ANY statement of the article's contents. The text was not retrieved and nothing about prepaid billing mechanics is asserted from it: not credit expiry, not refundability, not the order in which credit types are consumed, not what happens when a balance is depleted, not whether any automatic replenishment feature exists or how it behaves, and not any billing-mode default.

unretrievable_by_direct_fetch.resolution: Its EXISTENCE and currency were confirmed by web search (source S9, search_result_metadata_only). Its CONTENTS remain unretrieved: direct fetch is refused with 403 and the search returned no page text. Revision 1 recorded the contents as unavailable; that is still the correct record.

explicitly_unresolved: Whether a request to /v1/responses/input_tokens is billed at all. No source states it. This is the blocking unknown.
Whether failed, retried or rejected requests of either class are billed, and on what basis.

There is no established maximum for a single count attempt. The 1.088 USD figure used in the arithmetic is an ASSUMPTION (272,000 x $4/1M). L* = 272,000 is checked AFTER a count returns, so it cannot bound the billable size of a count request that is itself rejected as too large.

The mechanics of prepaid API billing. The only retrieved statements are that prepaid credits exist for an organization and that credit_balance_exhausted means the prepaid balance is depleted (source S4, hashed). Credit expiry, refundability, consumption order, depletion behaviour, any automatic replenishment feature, and any monthly/arrears alternative are NOT established by any source retrieved here.
WHEN money leaves this account. This follows from the billing mode and its mechanics, none of which is established. The user's question is recorded as unanswered rather than answered.

This account's billing mode, credit balance, usage tier, assigned monthly usage limit, configured hard spend limits, month-to-date spend, other traffic in the E9 project, whether any automatic credit replenishment is configured, tax treatment and contracting entity.
Whether the stated promotional rates will still apply at dispatch time.
what_a_successful_e9_would_establish: The charges for the specific count and generation calls that ran, as they appear in that account's usage records. It would NOT establish a per-call fee schedule, would NOT establish the treatment of failed or rejected calls, and would NOT license the study's arithmetic.
no_probe_authorized: This register does not propose, request or authorize a minimal paid probe. Resolving the count-charging question by making a paid request is a separate decision that is not sought here.

correction_note.issue: Revision 2 as first written recorded nine specific prepaid-billing facts against S9 (credit expiry after one year, non-refundability, free credits consumed first, non-instantaneous stop with a negative balance carried to the next purchase, an auto-recharge feature and an inconsistent default, payment-failure behaviour). Those statements were not in any retrieved source. The web search returned result metadata only; the facts came from the author's own recollection and were written as if sourced.
correction_note.action: All nine were removed from this register, from e9_financial_proposal_rev2_2026-09-09.md and from e9_review_response_rev2.md before these artifacts were saved. S9 now records only what the retrieval established. The prepaid mechanics and the timing of payment are listed as unresolved.
